title: GiraffeRun
description: A 2D top-down dodge-and-collect arcade game built with libGDX (Java). The player controls a giraffe character that must avoid falling rockets (bullets) while collecting crystals to advance through 3 progressively harder levels. The game features a shield ability and a teleport ability, full audio feedback, scrolling backgrounds, health management, and a game win / game over flow.
javaCompatibility: Java 8 source / target, runs on JVM 8+
features: 3-level progressive difficulty system (bullet spawn probability scales with level)
Player movement: keyboard left/right (S/D or Arrow keys)
Shield ability: activated by right-click, 3-second duration, 8-second cooldown, halves movement speed
Teleport ability: left-click to cursor position, 4-second cooldown
Falling drop system: BulletDrop (hazard, 2.5× speed), HealthDrop (heal up to max 5 HP), CrystalDrop (collect 5 to win level)
Scrolling parallax-style background per level (BG1.png, BG2.png, BG3.png)
Animated player sprite (alternating left/right movement frames at 0.15 s intervals)
Shield-mode sprite variants (giraffe with shield visual)
HUD: heart icons (health), crystal count, level number, shield cooldown timer, teleport cooldown timer
5 distinct sound effects: hit, shield hit, heal, collect crystal, teleport
Game Over and Game Win screens with replay/continue options
FitViewport (8×5 world units) ensuring resolution independence
Cross-platform fat-JAR distribution (Windows / macOS ARM & x64 / Linux x64)
Optional GraalVM native-image support (disabled by default)
techStack: libGDX 1.13.1 (core game framework: rendering, input, audio, math)
LWJGL3 backend (OpenGL via LWJGL 3 for desktop window and context)
Gradle 8.x (multi-module build, task: jar, dist, jarMac, jarLinux, jarWin)
Construo 1.7.1 (native executable wrapping with embedded JDK)
Eclipse / IntelliJ IDEA project support (via Gradle plugins)

modules.name: core
modules.role: Platform-agnostic game logic, screens, entities, and assets

modules.name: lwjgl3
modules.role: Desktop launcher, window configuration, platform bootstrap

architecture: Single-process desktop application. libGDX provides the game loop (render/update/dispose). The Main class acts as the application controller, sharing SpriteBatch, BitmapFont, FitViewport, and global game state (level, globalSpeed) across all screens. Screens are swapped via Game.setScreen(). Collision detection uses AABB (axis-aligned bounding box via libGDX Rectangle.overlaps). Asset loading is eager (no AssetManager) — all textures and sounds are loaded in screen constructors and disposed in hide()/dispose().
dataFlow: Player.update() → sprite bounds clamped to viewport → cooldown timers decremented
BackGround.update() → scrollY offset scrolled by globalSpeed+level → BackGround.render() tiles texture vertically
Win condition: crystalCollected >= 5 → level++ or GameWinScreen
Level transition: GameScreen → LoadScreen (SPACE) → new GameScreen(game) (level already incremented in Main)

textures: leftMoveShield.png, rightMoveShield.png (player run with shield active)
audio: teleportSound.wav (duplicate WAV, appears unused in code - only .mp3 loaded)

risks.description: No AssetManager used. All textures/sounds are loaded synchronously in constructors. This causes GPU stutters on screen transition and risks memory leaks if screens are re-created without proper disposal.

GameOverScreen and GameWinScreen do not dispose themeAudio, gameWinSound, or gameOverSound. Player sound assets (hitSound, healSound, etc.) have no dispose() call guard against null. GameScreen.dispose() also doesn't call shieldIcon.dispose() or teleportIcon.dispose().

Main.level and Main.globalSpeed are public mutable fields accessed directly from multiple screens. No encapsulation or state machine. Reset logic is fragmented between Player.reset() and GameScreen.reset().
CrystalDrop probability (1 - bulletProb - healthProb) can trend toward 0 at high levels, making the game impossible to win. At level 3: bulletProb = 0.65, healthProb = 0.16 → crystal chance = 0.19.

BackGround uses screen pixel height to convert texture height to world units. If window is resized, pixelToWorldY ratio changes but the scroll offset is not recalculated, potentially causing a visual tear or gap.

Move-left is mapped to S key (instead of A), which deviates from standard WASD and is inconsistent with move-right mapped to D. Arrow keys are also supported for right but not left (LEFT arrow maps to same branch as S).
GameWinScreen reuses MenuScreen.png as background instead of a dedicated win screen — a placeholder that reduces production quality.
FrontView.png and teleportSound.wav are in assets but never loaded/used in code. Adds unnecessary build artifact size.
BitmapFont is scaled using setScale() tied to viewport size. At very large resolutions the default BitmapFont becomes blurry. A distance-field font or FreeType font would be more scalable.

improvements: Introduce libGDX AssetManager for async background loading with a real loading screen progress bar
Add a dedicated GameState enum or state machine in Main to replace raw mutable fields
Implement a high-score / persistent save system using libGDX Preferences API
Add pause screen (ESC key) with resume/restart/quit options
Replace default BitmapFont with FreeType-generated or distance-field font for crisp text at all resolutions
Remap move-left to A key for standard WASD compliance; update FirstScreen instructions
Implement object pooling (libGDX Pool<Drop>) for drop entities to reduce GC pressure at high spawn rates
Refactor Player.dispose() to guard against already-disposed assets and call it in GameScreen.dispose()
Add shieldIcon and teleportIcon disposal in GameScreen.dispose()
Clamp crystal probability to a minimum (e.g., 0.15) to guarantee game is always winnable
Add music crossfade or per-screen music tracks (GameOverScreen is silent)
Introduce particle effects (libGDX Particles) for crystal collection and teleport visual feedback
